newsitem.title: USA: Orange County, Calif., to audit district attorney.
newsitem.headline: Orange County, Calif., to audit district attorney.

text.p: The Orange County, Calif., Board of Supervisors voted to conduct an audit of the county district attorney's office, county officials said on Thursday.
The district attorney's office has been conducting a broad probe of the county's bankruptcy, the largest municipal bankruptcy in U.S. history.
Last year, a county grand jury accused county Supervisors Roger Stanton and William Steiner of failing to oversee former county Treasurer Robert Citron and other county officials.
They were also accused of voting to issue county debt without making adequate inquiries into the need for the borrowings and whether the county could repay them.

In November, a state appeals court panel dismissed the misconduct charges against Stanton and Steiner, who had faced removal from office had the accusations been sustained by a jury. Earlier this week, the district attorney asked the panel to reconsider its decision.
Orange County filed for bankruptcy protection on Dec. 6, 1994, after sustaining losses of more than $1.6 billion on risky investments. The county emerged from bankruptcy in June.
A judge recently ordered Citron to spend one year in county jail and pay a $100,000 fine for his role in the county's bankruptcy.
